deadlines.description: Police remand maximum period: accused Rafiq Ahmed arrested on 20/02/2025; total police remand cannot exceed 15 days during investigation
deadlines.consequence: Any remand beyond 15 cumulative days is illegal; accused entitled to bail by default; any confession or statement obtained beyond this period is inadmissible; court must release accused on bail if chargesheet not filed within statutory period

deadlines.description: Chargesheet submission deadline: FIR filed 20/02/2025; drug case under Narcotics Control Act 2018 involving 500g Yaba (serious offence likely attracting above 10 years imprisonment) — chargesheet must be filed within 90 days of arrest under CrPC §167(2)
deadlines.consequence: If chargesheet not filed within 90 days, accused is entitled to default bail (bail by right); court must release accused on bail upon application; failure to do so violates fundamental right under Constitution Article 35(3)

deadlines.description: Investigation maximum period under Narcotics Control Act 2018: investigation from date of arrest (20/02/2025) must be completed within 60 days
deadlines.consequence: Investigation conducted beyond 60 days is procedurally defective; chargesheet filed after this deadline may be challenged; court may take adverse note of the delay; accused may seek discharge on grounds of procedural violation

deadlines.description: Trial completion deadline: if case has been committed to Speedy Trial Tribunal (applicable given serious narcotics offence), trial must complete within 90 days of committal
deadlines.consequence: If committal date is known and 90 days have elapsed, trial is in violation; court must record reasons for delay; prolonged delay can be ground for bail application citing Constitution Article 35(3); tribunal must explain non-compliance to High Court Division

deadlines.description: Trial completion deadline under general warrant case procedure: if charge has been framed, trial must complete within 180 days from date of charge framing or court must record reasons
deadlines.consequence: If charge framing date is known and 180 days have elapsed without trial completion, court is obligated to record written reasons; accused may apply for bail on grounds of inordinate delay; court may face supervisory action from High Court Division

deadlines.description: Constitutional right to speedy trial: arrest on 20/02/2025; as of today 25/04/2026, accused has been under process for approximately 429 days without confirmed trial completion
deadlines.consequence: Prolonged detention without trial conclusion constitutes violation of fundamental right to speedy trial; accused may file writ petition before High Court Division under Article 102 seeking bail or expedited trial; court may suo motu intervene
